html:
Walvis Bay, the only deep water port on the coast of Namibia, was held by Britain and then South Africa separately from the rest of the territory and was handed to Namibia only on 1 March 1994.

Britain annexed the bay in 1878 to keep it from other powers, and it became part of the Cape Colony, leaving the German colony to build ports at Lüderitz and Swakopmund. South Africa kept it when Namibia became independent in 1990, as a base and to keep control of Namibian trade.

After talks, the new democratic South Africa handed it over in 1994. It is now the main port of the country and a link in the Trans-Kalahari corridor to Botswana and South Africa.
sum: Walvis Bay, the only deep water port on the coast of Namibia, was held by Britain and then South Africa separately from the rest of the territory and was handed to Namibia only on 1 March 1994.
